podcast.title: The Grapes of Wrath Formation (1983)
podcast.body: The band was formed in Kelowna in 1983 by Kevin Kane, Chris Hooper, and Tom Hooper. "They came from Kelona in 1983. Three guys here, Kevin Kane and Chris and Tom Hooper."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost CanRock Bands of the 90s: Part 2

podcast.title: Nettwerk Records Deal (1987)
podcast.body: By 1987, the band secured a deal with Nettwerk Records in Vancouver, leading to the recording of two highly acclaimed albums. "By 1987 they had a deal with network records in Vancouver and recorded a couple of very well-received albums."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost CanRock Bands of the 90s: Part 2

podcast.title: Rise in 1991
podcast.body: Grapes of Wrath began their rise in 1991, becoming part of a new crop of Canadian artists gaining prominence. Their emergence signaled the expansion of the "Can Rock explosion" beyond its initial wave. "1991, so the beginning of the rise of the Barodicad Ladies, Spirit of the West, Sarah McLaughlin, Crash Vegas, Crash Test Dummies, and Grapes of Wrath."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Roots of the 90s CanRock Explosion

podcast.title: Partial Reunion and Acoustic Gigs (1999)
podcast.body: A partial reunion of the band occurred in 1999, resulting in the *Field Trip* album, followed by a series of acoustic performances. "a partial grapes of Wrath reunion in 1999 which resulted in an album entitled Field Trip, Acoustic Gigs followed."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost CanRock Bands of the 90s: Part 2

podcast.title: Full Reunion (2010)
podcast.body: The Grapes of Wrath achieved a full reunion in 2010, which has largely remained intact since. "before a full reunion in 2010 and that reunion has mostly stuck."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost CanRock Bands of the 90s: Part 2

podcast.title: Early 1990s Prime Time Success
podcast.body: Grapes of Wrath were listed as one of the Canadian bands that gained "prime time" attention in the early 1990s. "The early 90s were pretty amazing with a long list of Canadian bands getting a shot at prime time. We had moist, the watchman, lowest of the low, sons of freedom, grapes of wrath, rhymes with orange, pure Gandarva's limb lifter."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 90s Part 8: The CanRock Revolution

podcast.title: Ginger Formation
podcast.body: The remaining members of The Grapes of Wrath continued performing under the name Ginger and experienced some success for a period. "while the rest of the group continued under the name Ginger and they did all right for a bit."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost CanRock Bands of the 90s: Part 2

podcast.title: Kevin Kane's Solo Career
podcast.body: After the band's split, Kevin Kane pursued a solo career. "Kevin went solo."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost CanRock Bands of the 90s: Part 2

podcast.title: Radio Presence (Late 1980s-Early 1990s)
podcast.body: The band released many singles during this period and became a consistent presence on radio stations. "There were plenty of singles during that period. But Grapes of Wrath became a staple on the radio for a while."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost CanRock Bands of the 90s: Part 2

podcast.title: The Grapes of Wrath Split (Reasons)
podcast.body: The band eventually split, possibly due to creative differences or an issue regarding their name. It was suggested that the people entrusted with the legacy of John Steinbeck's novel *The Grapes of Wrath* were not pleased to share the name with the band. "But then the band split. It might have been creative differences or it might have been an issue over their name."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
